## Parties – general

## 19.1 Any number of claimants or defendants may be joined as parties to a claim. ## I ADDITION AND SUBSTITUTION OF PARTIES

## Change of parties – general

## 19.2

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.2] (1) This rule applies where a party is to be added or substituted except where the case falls within rule 19.6 (special provisions about changing parties after the end of a relevant limitation period (GL) ). [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.2] (2) The court may order a person to be added as a new party if –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.2] (a) it is desirable to add the new party so that the court can resolve all the matters in dispute in the proceedings; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.2] (b) there is an issue involving the new party and an existing party which is connected to the matters in dispute in the proceedings, and it is desirable to add the new party so that the court can resolve that issue. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.2] (3) The court may order any person to cease to be a party if it is not desirable for that person to be a party to the proceedings. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.2] (4) The court may order a new party to be substituted for an existing one if –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.2] (a) the existing party’s interest or liability has passed to the new party;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.2] (b) it is desirable to substitute the new party so that the court can resolve the matters in dispute in the proceedings. ## Provisions applicable where two or more persons are jointly entitled to a remedy

## 19.3

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.3] (1) All persons jointly entitled to the remedy claimed by a claimant must be parties unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.3] (2) If any such person does not agree to be a claimant, he must be made a defendant, unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.3] (3) This rule does not apply in probate proceedings. ## Procedure for adding and substituting parties

## 19.4

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (1) The court’s permission is required to remove, add or substitute a party, unless the claim form has not been served. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (2) An application for permission under paragraph (1)—

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (a) may be made by—

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (i) an existing party; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (ii) a person who wishes to become a party; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (b) must be—

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (i) supported by evidence; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (ii) made under Part 23. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (3) An application for an order under rule 19.2(4) –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (a) may be made without notice; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (b) must be supported by evidence. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (4) Nobody may be added or substituted as a claimant unless –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (a) they have given their consent in writing; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (b) that consent, and the proposed amended claim form and particulars of claim, have been filed with the court. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (5) If an order is made adding or substituting a person as a claimant prior to the filing of their consent—

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (a) the order; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (b) the addition or substitution of the new party as claimant,

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] shall not take effect until the signed, written consent of the new claimant is filed. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (6) The Commissioners for HM Revenue and Customs may, where a dispute between other parties may have tax consequences, be added as party to proceedings if they consent in writing. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (7) An order for the removal, addition or substitution of a party must be served on—

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (a) all parties to the proceedings; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (b) any other person affected by the order. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (8) When the court makes an order for the removal, addition or substitution of a party, it may give consequential directions. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (9) A new defendant does not become a party to the proceedings until the amended claim form has been served on them. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (10) A party applying to add a new party by amendment shall be responsible for the costs of and arising from the amendment unless the court decides otherwise. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.4] (11) The court may remove, add or substitute parties in existing proceedings on its own initiative. ## Human Rights

## 19.5

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (1) The court may not make a declaration of incompatibility in accordance with section 4 of the Human Rights Act 1998(1) unless 21 days’ notice, or such other period of notice as the court directs, has been given to the Crown by the claimant. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (2) Where a claim is made under section 9 of the Human Rights Act 1998 for damages in respect of a judicial act—

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (a) that claim, including details of the judicial act, must be set out in the statement of case or the appeal notice; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (b) notice must be given to the Crown. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (3) The court may at any time consider whether notice under paragraph (1) or (2) should be given to the Crown and give directions as to the content and service of such notice. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (4) A notice served on the Crown must be served on—

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (a) the person named in the list published under section 17 of the Crown Proceedings Act 1947(2) (which is annexed to Practice Direction 66);

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (b) Senedd Cymru, in the circumstances described in the National Assembly for Wales (Transfer of Functions) (No. 2) Order 2000(3);

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (c) the Treasury Solicitor on behalf of the Lord Chancellor, in respect of a claim under section 9 of the Human Rights Act 1998, except where the judicial act is of a Court-Martial when service must be on the Treasury Solicitor on behalf of the Secretary of State for Defence;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (d) all parties. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (5) Where notice has been given to the Crown, a Minister or other person permitted by the Human Rights Act 1998 shall be joined as a party on notifying their consent to the court and all other parties. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (6) Where the Minister has, under section 5(2)(a) of the Human Rights Act 1998, nominated a person to be joined, the notice consenting to be joined must be accompanied by the written nomination. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.5] (7) Where paragraph (2) applies and the appropriate person has not applied to be joined as a party within 21 days, or such other period as the court directs, after the notice is served, the court may join the appropriate person as a party. ## 19.6

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (1) This rule applies to a change of parties after the end of a period of limitation under –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (a) the Limitation Act 1980 1 ;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (b) the Foreign Limitation Periods Act 1984 2 ; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (c) any other enactment which allows such a change, or under which such a change is allowed. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (2) The court may add or substitute a party only if –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (a) the relevant limitation period (GL) was current when the proceedings were started; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (b) the addition or substitution is necessary. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (3) The addition or substitution of a party is necessary only if the court is satisfied that –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (a) the new party is to be substituted for a party who was named in the claim form in mistake for the new party;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (b) the claim cannot properly be carried on by or against the original party unless the new party is added or substituted as claimant or defendant; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (c) the original party has died or had a bankruptcy order made against them and their interest or liability has passed to the new party. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (4) In addition, in a claim for personal injuries the court may add or substitute a party where it directs that –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (a)

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (i) section 11 (special time limit for claims for personal injuries); or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (ii) section 12 (special time limit for claims under fatal accidents legislation), of the Limitation Act 1980 shall not apply to the claim by or against the new party; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.6] (b) the issue of whether those sections apply shall be determined at trial. ## Special rules about parties in claims for wrongful interference with goods

## 19.7

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.7] (1) A claimant in a claim for wrongful interference with goods must, in the particulars of claim, state the name and address of every person who, to the claimant’s knowledge, has or claims an interest in the goods and who is not a party to the claim. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.7] (2) A defendant to a claim for wrongful interference with goods may apply for a direction that another person be made a party to the claim to establish whether the other person –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.7] (a) has a better right to the goods than the claimant; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.7] (b) has a claim which might render the defendant doubly liable under section 7 of the Torts (Interference with Goods) Act 1977(a). [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.7] (3) Where the person referred to in paragraph (2) fails to attend the hearing of the application, or comply with any directions, the court may order that person is deprived of any claim against the defendant in respect of the goods. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.7] (4) The application notice must be served on all parties and on the person referred to in paragraph (2). ## II REPRESENTATIVE PARTIES

## Representative parties with same interest

## 19.8

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.8] (1) Where more than one person has the same interest in a claim –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.8] (a) the claim may be begun; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.8] (b) the court may order that the claim be continued,

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.8] by or against one or more of the persons who have the same interest as representatives of any other persons who have that interest. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.8] (2) The court may direct that a person may not act as a representative. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.8] (3) Any party may apply to the court for an order under paragraph (2). [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.8] (4) Unless the court otherwise directs any judgment or order given in a claim in which a party is acting as a representative under this rule –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.8] (a) is binding on all persons represented in the claim; but

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.8] (b) may only be enforced by or against a person who is not a party to the claim with the permission of the court. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.8] (5) This rule does not apply to a claim to which rule 19.9 applies. ## Representation of interested persons who cannot be ascertained etc. ## 19.9

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (1) This rule applies to claims about –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (a) the estate of a deceased person;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (b) property subject to a trust; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (c) the meaning of a document, including a statute. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (2) The court may make an order appointing a person to represent any other person or persons in the claim where the person or persons to be represented –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (a) are unborn;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (b) cannot be found;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (c) cannot easily be ascertained; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (d) are a class of persons who have the same interest in a claim and –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (i) one or more members of that class are within sub-paragraphs (a), (b) or (c); or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (ii) to appoint a representative would further the overriding objective. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (3) An application for an order under paragraph (2) –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (a) may be made by –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (i) any person who seeks to be appointed under the order; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (ii) any party to the claim; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (b) may be made at any time before or after the claim has started. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (4) An application notice for an order under paragraph (2) must be served on –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (a) all parties to the claim, if the claim has started;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (b) the person sought to be appointed, if that person is not the applicant or a party to the claim; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (c) any other person as directed by the court. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (5) The court’s approval is required to settle a claim in which a party is acting as a representative under this rule. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (6) The court may approve a settlement where it is satisfied that the settlement is for the benefit of all the represented persons. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (7) Unless the court otherwise directs, any judgment or order given in a claim in which a party is acting as a representative under this rule –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (a) is binding on all persons represented in the claim; but

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.9] (b) may only be enforced by or against a person who is not a party to the claim with the permission of the court. ## Representation of beneficiaries by trustees etc. ## 19.10

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.10] (1) A claim may be brought by or against trustees, executors or administrators in that capacity without adding as parties any persons who have a beneficial interest in the trust or estate (‘the beneficiaries’). [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.10] (2) Any judgment or order given or made in the claim is binding on the beneficiaries unless the court orders otherwise in the same or other proceedings. ## Postal Services Act 2000

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > Postal Services Act 2000] 19.11 A copy of an application notice under section 92 of the Postal Services Act 2000(4) for permission to bring proceedings in the name of the sender or addressee of a postal packet or their personal representative must be served on the universal service provider and on the person in whose name the applicant seeks to bring the proceedings. ## Death

## 19.12

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (1) Where a person who had an interest in a claim has died and that person has no personal representative the court may order –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (a) the claim to proceed in the absence of a person representing the estate of the deceased; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (b) a person to be appointed to represent the estate of the deceased. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (2) Where a defendant against whom a claim could have been brought has died and –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (a) a grant of probate or administration has been made, the claim must be brought against the persons who are the personal representatives of the deceased;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (b) a grant of probate or administration has not been made –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (i) the claim must be brought against ‘the estate of’ the deceased; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (ii) the claimant must apply to the court for an order appointing a person to represent the estate of the deceased in the claim. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (3) A claim shall be treated as having been brought against ‘the estate of’ the deceased in accordance with paragraph (2)(b)(i) where –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (a) the claim is brought against the ‘personal representatives’ of the deceased but a grant of probate or administration has not been made; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (b) the person against whom the claim was brought was dead when the claim was started. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (4) Before making an order under this rule, the court may direct notice of the application to be given to any other person with an interest in the claim. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.12] (5) Where an order has been made under paragraphs (1) or (2)(b)(ii) any judgment or order made or given in the claim is binding on the estate of the deceased. ## Power to make judgements binding on non-parties

## 19.13

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (1) This rule applies to any claim relating to –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (a) the estate of a deceased person;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (b) property subject to a trust; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (c) the sale of any property. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (2) The court may at any time direct that notice of –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (a) the claim; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (b) any judgment or order given in the claim,

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] be served on any person who is not a party but who is or may be affected by it. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (3) An application under this rule –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (a) may be made without notice; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (b) must be supported by written evidence which includes the reasons why the person to be served should be bound by the judgment in the claim. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (4) Unless the court orders otherwise –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (a) a notice of a claim or of a judgment or order under this rule must be –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (i) in the prescribed form;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (ii) issued by the court; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (iii) accompanied by a form of acknowledgment of service with any necessary modifications;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (b) a notice of a claim must also be accompanied by –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (i) a copy of the claim form; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (ii) such other statements of case, witness statements or affidavits as the court may direct; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (c) a notice of a judgment or order must also be accompanied by a copy of the judgment or order. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (5) If a person served with notice of a claim files an acknowledgment of service of the notice within 14 days they will become a party to the claim. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (6) If a person served with notice of a claim does not acknowledge service of the notice they will be bound by any judgment given in the claim as if they were a party. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (7) If, after service of a notice of a claim on a person, the claim form is amended so as substantially to alter the relief claimed, the court may direct that a judgment shall not bind that person unless a further notice, together with a copy of the amended claim form, is served on them. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (8) Any person served with a notice of a judgment or order under this rule –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (a) shall be bound by the judgment or order as if they had been a party to the claim; but

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (b) may, provided they acknowledges service –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (i) within 28 days after the notice is served on them, apply to the court to set aside or vary the judgment or order; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (ii) take part in any proceedings relating to the judgment or order. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (9) The following rules of Part 10 (acknowledgment of service) apply –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (b) rule 10.5, subject to the modification that references to the defendant are to be read as references to the person served with the notice. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.13] (10) A notice under this rule is issued on the date entered on the notice by the court. ## Derivative claims – how started

## 19.14

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.14] (1) This rule –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.14] (a) applies to a derivative claim (where a company, other body corporate or trade union is alleged to be entitled to claim a remedy, and a claim is made by a member of it for it to be given that remedy), whether under Chapter 1 of Part 11 of the Companies Act 2006 3 or otherwise; but

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.14] (b) does not apply to a claim made pursuant to an order under section 996 of that Act. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.14] (2) A derivative claim must be started by a claim form headed “Derivative Claim”. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.14] (3) The company, body corporate or trade union for the benefit of which a remedy is sought must be made a defendant to the claim. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.14] (4) After the issue of the claim form, the claimant must not take any further step in the proceedings without the permission of the court, other than –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.14] (a) a step permitted or required by rule 19.15 or 19.17; or

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.14] (b) making an urgent application for interim relief. ## Derivative claims under Chapter 1 of Part 11 of the Companies Act 2006 – application for permission

## 19.15

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.15] (1) In this rule –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.15] ‘the Act’ means the Companies Act 2006;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.15] ‘derivative claim’ means a derivative claim under Chapter 1 of Part 11 of the Act;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.15] ‘permission application’ means an application referred to in section 261(1), 262(2) or 264(2) of the Act;

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.15] ‘the company’ means the company for the benefit of which the derivative claim is brought. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.15] (2) When the claim form for a derivative claim is issued, the claimant must file –

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.15] (a) an application notice under Part 23 for permission to continue the claim; and

[PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.15] (b) the written evidence on which the claimant relies in support of the permission application. [PART 19 – PARTIES AND GROUP LITIGATION > 19.15] (3) The claimant must not make the company a respondent to the permission application.
